$comment: Inbound email -- Tynn #11. Resend signs every webhook with Svix (https://resend.com/docs/webhooks/verify-webhooks-requests, checked 2026-09-15): the signed content is `{svix-id}.{svix-timestamp}.{body}`, HMAC-SHA256, the signature base64 in `svix-signature` as a SPACE-separated list of `v1,<sig>` of which any may match, and the secret is `whsec_<base64>` whose HMAC key is the DECODED remainder. Three things no earlier provider needed, each in fancy-connector-core 0.9.0: an `{id}` payload slot, `secretEncoding` + `secretPrefix`, and every signature offered rather than the first. The event itself carries METADATA ONLY -- "Webhooks do not include the email body, headers, or attachments" -- so `then` names the read that fetches the email first.
title: Email received
description: Start when an email arrives at one of your Resend receiving addresses, with the email read in full.
setup: Point a receiving domain's MX record at Resend, then in the Resend dashboard (Webhooks → Add webhook) point an endpoint at the route your host mounts for this trigger and subscribe it to email.received. Put the endpoint's signing secret -- shown as whsec_… -- on the connection as `webhookSecret`, exactly as shown.

verification.$toleranceComment: Svix leaves the replay window to the implementer and its own libraries reject a timestamp more than five minutes from now; this connector matches them.
verification.$payloadComment: Svix signs `{svix-id}.{svix-timestamp}.{rawBody}` -- the delivery's own id is part of the signed content, so a delivery without its svix-id header is refused by name rather than signed with a hole. The body must be the bytes EXACTLY as received.

header.$comment: `v1,<base64> v1,<base64>` -- several during a secret rotation, and Svix says yours must match ONE of them. Every `v1` is offered to the verifier; the first-only rule that Stripe's header once carried refused a whole roll.

verification.$secretComment: The connection stores the secret as Resend shows it, `whsec_…`. The verifier strips the prefix and base64-decodes the rest into the HMAC key -- raw bytes, half of which are not UTF-8. Signing with the text instead never matches and reads exactly like a wrong secret, which is why the core does the decoding and refuses a malformed secret by name.

then.$comment: The run's FIRST step, after the host has verified the delivery and answered Resend: email_get with the delivery's email_id, published under `email`. A failed read fails the run with the core's classification -- a delivery whose email cannot be read must not start a flow that assumes it was. `verdicts: null` is said rather than left absent: Resend exposes no SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdicts on a received email (checked 2026-09-14), and an author looking for them must find a null, not a missing key that reads like a field nobody wired. Agreed with Fancy 2026-09-15.

outputShape.description: Always email.received on this trigger.
ISO 8601, when the webhook was sent.
The received email's id. Resend redelivers on failure -- dedupe on this.
ISO 8601, when Resend received the email.
The sender's address, bare.
Recipient addresses.
Carbon-copy addresses; empty when none.
Blind-copy addresses; empty when none.
Addresses the email was forwarded for, when it reached Resend through a forward.
The RFC 5322 Message-ID, angle brackets included.
The subject line.
Attachment metadata as the delivery carries it: id, filename, content_type, content_disposition, content_id. No size, no URL -- `email.attachments` has the size, attachment_get has the URL.
The email, read in full after the delivery: its id, equal to data.email_id.
The sender's address, bare.
Recipient addresses.
Carbon-copy addresses; empty when none.
Blind-copy addresses; empty when none.
Reply-To addresses; empty when none.
The subject line.
ISO 8601, when Resend received it.
The HTML body, when the email carried one.
How inline images are referenced in `email.html`: data_uri or cid.
The plain-text body. NULL when the email carried only HTML -- branch on it before reading.
The email's headers as a map, lower-cased names.
Addresses the email was forwarded for.
The RFC 5322 Message-ID, angle brackets included. Dedupe across providers on this.
A signed URL for the raw MIME message; expires at email.raw.expires_at. NULL when Resend kept no raw copy.
ISO 8601 expiry of email.raw.download_url.
The attachments' metadata WITH size: id, filename, content_type, content_disposition, content_id, size. attachment_get turns an id into a download URL.
Always null. Resend exposes no SPF, DKIM or DMARC verdicts on a received email; the key is here so a flow that wants them finds an explicit nothing rather than a missing field.
